descriptionChirho: General sense of possession, ownership, or having something at one's disposal, across all tenses, moods, persons, and participial forms of the active voice: 'has/have/had/will have/having/to have.' English 'has, have, had, having,' Spanish 'tiene, tengo, tenía, tener, teniendo,' Arabic لَهُ / لَكُمْ / لَنا / كَانَ لَهُ, Korean 가지다 / 가졌다 / 가진, Swahili -na / nina / ana / wana.

To hold someone or something in a certain estimation, to consider or regard as; used with a double accusative or predicate complement meaning 'they held him as a prophet / they regarded him as.' English 'they held, they were holding (as),' Spanish 'lo tenían (por), tenían,' Hindi मानते थे (they considered), Arabic يَعتَبِرونَ / كَانُوا يَحْسِبُونَهُ (they were reckoning him), Korean 여기다 / 여겼다 (to regard), Swahili walimhesabu (they counted him).

To physically hold, grasp, seize, or metaphorically hold fast to and cling to something; emphasis on retention or grip rather than mere possession. English 'hold, hold fast,' Spanish 'ten, tened (hold!),' Hindi पकड़ा था (had grabbed), Arabic تَمَسَّكْ / مُتَمَسِّكينَ (hold firmly / clinging), Korean 가져라 (take hold!), Swahili shika / wakiishikilia (grasp / they were clinging).

Middle/passive participle τῇ ἐχομένῃ used as a temporal adjective meaning 'the following, the next (day)'; a frozen participial construction distinct from active possession. English 'following,' Spanish 'siguiente,' Hindi अगले (next), Arabic التَّالِي (the next), Korean 다음 (next), Swahili inayofuata (that which follows).

Middle/passive participle τὰς ἐχομένας used as a spatial adjective meaning 'neighboring, nearby, adjacent'; another frozen participial construction. English 'neighboring,' Spanish 'cercanas,' Hindi पास के (nearby), Arabic المُجَاوِرَة (neighboring), Korean 인근의 (nearby), Swahili za karibu (those nearby).

Idiomatic expression ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχω meaning 'to have in the womb, to be pregnant'; a specialized collocation where ἔχω combines with the prepositional phrase to form a distinct lexical unit. English 'having (in womb),' Spanish 'teniendo / que tienen (embarazada),' Hindi रखनेवालियों / धारण करेगी (bearing), Arabic حَامِلَة / حَامِلَاتٍ / سَتَحْمِلُ (pregnant / will conceive), Korean 가진 여자에게 (to a woman having [child]), Swahili mimba (pregnancy).

Quasi-copular use of ἔχω with an adverb or prepositional phrase to express being in a state or condition (e.g., καλῶς ἔχω 'I am well,' κακῶς ἔχοντες 'those who are sick'); the verb functions as 'to be' rather than 'to have.' English 'is, are, to be,' Spanish 'está, están, ser,' Hindi हैं / बीमार (are / sick), Arabic حالُهُم / هِيَ / أَنا (their condition / she is / I am), Korean 있는지 / 있습니다 (being), Swahili wako / yuko (they are / he/she is).
